figure_coverage.exact_caption_method: Verbatim PyMuPDF block text, retaining printed line-break hyphenation and flattened math subscripts. Captions are from reviewed PDF, not presumed from current source.

figure_diagnostics.exact_caption_pdf_text:
Figure 1: Skill routing with a task applicability pred-
icate. The skill is appropriately selected for task q1
because the task asks about the price for a specific trad-
ing day. The skill is not accepted for task q2 because it
asks for the price between a range of years.
figure_diagnostics.inspection_method: vision_analyze full-page render; Figures 1 and 2 additionally inspected using cropped zooms
figure_diagnostics.current_state: Column-width raster diagram: two coffee-price tasks flow through Coffee Price Data Single-Day Analysis and its predicate to green Selected/True and red Not Selected/False boxes. The single-day task asks whether May 19, 2021 was bullish or bearish; the multi-year task asks for the highest price between 2019 and 2021. Caption captures the single-day/range distinction. It illustrates applicability, not the proposed replay/gate update.

measured_fonts_pt.reason: Raster text, not PDF text spans

problems: Internal task/predicate prose is visibly much smaller than the adjacent 10 pt caption at column width; zoom makes it decipherable but does not establish print readability.
Color is not the sole encoding: Selected/Not Selected and True/False are redundant labels.
The contribution is not explained here; making Figure 1 a method teaser is optional editorial advice, not ACL policy.
figure_diagnostics.recommendation: Shorten task and predicate labels; allocate more vertical space or redraw as a vector while retaining the same semantics. Optionally add an explicit link to the replay/gate mechanism rather than replacing this explanatory example.

figure_diagnostics.exact_caption_pdf_text:
Figure 2: RouterBSI’s bayes self-improvement algorithm of predicate psk for the skill sk in top k. Routing failures
drive revisions selected which are selected based on their bounded replay error using Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR).
Selected candidate is discarded by the held-out validation gate if its validation error is higher than the initial predicate
psi.
figure_diagnostics.inspection_method: vision_analyze full-page render; Figures 1 and 2 additionally inspected using cropped zooms
figure_diagnostics.current_state: Full-width raster flowchart with Skill Routing, Update Proposal, and Update Selection. Markdown-table formatting falsely activates CSV Data Analysis; failure feedback generates three predicates. MBR box lists pf=0.50, m1=0.25, m2=0.00 selected, m3=0.25; gate displays psi=0.60 > m*=0.45 and Passed. Lower loop returns to predicate evaluation. Both Success and Failure paths are present.

measured_fonts_pt.reason: Raster text, no extractable font size

problems: The printed caption omits equality from gate rejection whereas PDF p4 states higher or equal and a strict less-than admission rule.
Numbers are written as predicates equal to scores instead of explicitly named replay/validation risks, and not identified as illustrative.
Routing success/failure edge conditions are not explicitly labeled; the shown True decision is not sufficient by itself to establish success.
Diagram is legible at full width; no clipping observed. Red/green states have text labels.
figure_diagnostics.recommendation: Align the caption with strict admission; label score expressions R_replay and R_v and mark the example illustrative. Optionally label branches correct/incorrect relative to required-skill labels.

figure_diagnostics.exact_caption_pdf_text:
Figure 3: Retention of required skills averaged across
retrievers: BM25, Vector, and SkillSight. The baseline
averages the base retrievers used to retrieve the initial
top 50 skill. RouterBSI preserves the most required
skills as the cutoff k decreases.
figure_diagnostics.inspection_method: vision_analyze full-page render; Figures 1 and 2 additionally inspected using cropped zooms
figure_diagnostics.current_state: Six normalized retention curves at equally spaced categorical cutoffs 50,25,10,5,1. RouterBSI stays highest; different colors, markers and line patterns aid identification. Legend above the plotting area, no error bands. All curves begin at 100%.
problems: Caption does not define Ret@k as a ratio of task-mean recalls normalized by each method/retriever own Recall@50; this definition is relegated to Appendix F.
SkillDAG uses an expanded pool: normalized retention does not mean a controlled common-candidate comparison or absolute recovery of the full gold set.
Legend/axes are readable at the reviewed render; no clipping observed.
figure_diagnostics.recommendation: Add the normalization and equal-across-retrievers aggregation in the caption or immediate main text; explicitly distinguish absolute recall and method-specific pool coverage. Keep categorical cutoffs labeled.

figure_diagnostics.exact_caption_pdf_text:
Figure 4: Downstream success rates averaged equally across BM25, Vector, and SkillSight. Lines mark LLM Direct
and Oracle. RouterBSItop-5 outperforms strict selection and most other approaches oracle performance.
figure_diagnostics.inspection_method: vision_analyze full-page render; Figures 1 and 2 additionally inspected using cropped zooms
figure_diagnostics.current_state: Full-width seven-bar downstream success plot with values 0.580,0.562,0.602,0.631,0.551,0.596,0.611. Dashed Direct=0.507 and dash-dot Oracle=0.638 lines; success-rate axis starts at 0.4. SkillDAG is the highest bar. All bars use the same blue; method identity uses text.
problems: Despite full width, rotated category labels and especially strict/top-5 subscripts are small relative to surrounding body/caption. No clipping seen.

Truncated bar baseline visually amplifies differences; precise labels make the scale recoverable. A dot plot or zero-based bars would be clearer, but is an editorial recommendation, not a policy violation.
Caption ends with the malformed phrase most other approaches oracle performance. It should explicitly preserve the SkillDAG exception and not suggest exceeding oracle.
No uncertainty displayed; do not infer statistical significance from these bars.
figure_diagnostics.recommendation: Use a larger-font dot plot or larger-font zero-based bars, spell out strict/top-5 labels, and repair the caption with the displayed means and SkillDAG/oracle comparison.

figure_diagnostics.exact_caption_pdf_text:
Figure 5: Ablation of MBR replay and held-out vali-
dation gate comparing routing performance. The lines
and areas represent the standard mean and variation,
respectively across three runs starting from the same
initial predicates at iteration 0. Combining replay and
gating yields the strongest final routing performance.
figure_diagnostics.inspection_method: vision_analyze full-page render; Figures 1 and 2 additionally inspected using cropped zooms
figure_diagnostics.current_state: Four test nDCG@1 trajectories over iterations 0–10 with narrow shaded bands. Both Enabled finishes highest, Only MBR next, Only Gate next, Both Disabled lowest. Color, marker and line-style differences provide redundant distinctions. No clipping.
problems: Caption calls lines/areas standard mean and variation, not an identifiable uncertainty statistic. Source provenance and Appendix Table 11 establish mean ± one population standard deviation across three runs (not a CI).
Caption does not identify Qwen3.5 4B, SkillSight, test split or task weighting.

Same initial predicates does not establish identical initial measured outcomes or independently seeded runs; appendix reports differing initial scores and one recorded seed. No unsupported accusation of unequal predicate initialization is made.
figure_diagnostics.recommendation: State test nDCG@1, backbone/retriever, 748-task within-run weighting, three-run mean and ±1 population SD using rounded source variance. Do not call bands confidence intervals or runs different seeds.

figure_diagnostics.exact_caption_pdf_text:
Figure 6: Impact of MBR replay and held-out valida-
tion gate on routing performance (nDCG@1) and token
usage. Both enabled gives the strongest performance.
MBR alone uses fewer tokens at a performance cost.
figure_diagnostics.inspection_method: vision_analyze full-page render; Figures 1 and 2 additionally inspected using cropped zooms
figure_diagnostics.current_state: Four-point performance/token scatter with distinct diamond, triangle, circle and square symbols. Both Enabled is top-right, Only MBR next in quality and cost; Both Disabled and Only Gate lower-left. No error bars; visibly legible 8/9 pt labels.
problems: Horizontal axis says Total Token Usage although provenance explicitly records known-only incomplete run-local costs excluding external/shared initialization.

Main caption does not explain this is a single-run comparison, unlike the three-run Figure 5; main text juxtaposes the two without the population distinction. Appendix Table 12 provides single-run status and unknown-attempt counts.
No uncertainty or complete economic-cost claim is established.
figure_diagnostics.recommendation: Rename axis Known recorded tokens (millions), state phase scope/exclusions and unknown usage, and label single-run endpoint evidence in main caption or prose.

figure_diagnostics.exact_caption_pdf_text:
Figure 7:
Initial and optimized routing perfor-
mance (nDCG@1) comparison between different LLM-
backbones using SkillSight as the retriever. Stronger
backbones improve initialization, while optimization
brings smaller model Qwen3.5 4B close to the opti-
mized performance of GPT-OSS 120B.
figure_diagnostics.inspection_method: vision_analyze full-page render; Figures 1 and 2 additionally inspected using cropped zooms
figure_diagnostics.current_state: Grouped initial/optimized bars for Qwen3.5 4B (0.520/0.742), Qwen3.8 27B (0.635/0.802), GPT-OSS 120B (0.686/0.745), plus shared gray SkillSight reference 0.471. Initial bars hatched, final bars solid; zero-based axis; value labels readable. No error bars.
problems: No uncertainty estimated; provenance says historical candidates are preserved, not a controlled common-candidate comparison.

The surrounding claim of a plateau that cannot be overcome by more capable LLMs exceeds what three uncontrolled model endpoints establish. Nonmonotonic optimized scores alone do not prove an inherent capacity ceiling.
Gray SkillSight reference visually resembles the generic solid optimized legend key; its separate x-axis label prevents a severe ambiguity but a baseline note would help.
figure_diagnostics.recommendation: Add single-run/existing-candidate qualification and reference-bar meaning. Replace the capacity-ceiling assertion with the observed nonmonotonicity and need for controlled comparison.

figure_diagnostics.exact_caption_pdf_text:
Figure 8: Recorded tokens and routing performance at different candidate-pool sizes. Blue shades distinguish Top-K
settings, which specify how many retrieved candidates are evaluated rather than how many skills are ultimately
selected.
figure_diagnostics.inspection_method: vision_analyze full-page render; Figures 1 and 2 additionally inspected using cropped zooms
figure_diagnostics.current_state: Full-width Appendix scatter: three candidate pool sizes (Top-K 10,25,50) shown by light-to-dark blue circles; larger pools have higher recorded tokens and final nDCG@10. Caption correctly distinguishes number of evaluated candidates from final selected skills. No clipping; comfortably larger labels than most main figures.
problems: Same-color-family circles rely on shade to map Top-K identity; direct labels or distinct shapes would strengthen accessibility.
Axis Total Token Usage is stronger than caption Recorded tokens; provenance says incomplete known-only run-local totals excluding shared/external initialization.
No uncertainty displayed; three observed pool sizes do not establish a general scaling law.
figure_diagnostics.recommendation: Use known-recorded-token wording consistently, state single-run scope if confirmed by the associated result table, and directly label the three points or use three marker shapes.

issues.problem: The main retention caption omits the normalization required to interpret its headline curve.
reasoning_chain: Step 1: All curves begin at 100%, whereas Appendix F defines Ret@k as a ratio of task-averaged recalls, per method/retriever, using that method own Recall@50.
Step 2: SkillDAG expands its pool, so curves do not share the same denominator/candidate coverage.
Step 3: Readers of the main paper can mistake relative retention for absolute gold-skill recall.
issues.predicted_reviewer_objection: Simulated: The main retention caption omits the normalization required to interpret its headline curve.

fix.instruction: Add the Appendix F definition to the main caption or adjacent main text, including per-method denominator and equal-across-retrievers averaging.
fix.target_text: Ret@k is 100 × Recall@k / Recall@50, using task-averaged recalls for each method and retriever, then averaged equally over BM25, Vector, and SkillSight. Each method uses its own Recall@50 denominator; SkillDAG uses its expanded pool. Thus these curves compare normalized retention rather than absolute recall.
required_inputs: Author confirmation of revision stage and permission before any manuscript edits
acceptance_criteria: Caption/main text defines ratio-of-means, not mean per-task ratio.
